title: Brewers Beat Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to Win First World Series Title
dek: Milwaukee closed out the series at Tropicana Field on Wednesday night, a franchise first, one night after Tampa Bay forced Game 5 with a 12th-inning walk-off.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Interior view of Tropicana Field, the Tampa Bay Rays' home ballpark, from the upper deck

keyPoints: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 of the World Series on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at Tropicana Field.
ESPN's final score report describes it as the Brewers' first World Series title in franchise history.
Tampa Bay had forced Game 5 the night before with a 4-3 win in 12 innings in Game 4, after Milwaukee had taken a 3-0 series lead.
body:
The Milwaukee Brewers won the World Series on Wednesday night, beating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. It is the first championship in the franchise's history, according to ESPN's final score report for the game.

## Closing out the series

The Rays had kept the series alive the night before. Ben Williamson's walk-off single in the bottom of the 12th inning gave Tampa Bay a 4-3 win in Game 4, after Cooper Pratt had hit a tiebreaking home run for Milwaukee in the top of the same inning, according to the Associated Press. The win made Tampa Bay the fourth team in World Series history to avoid elimination with an extra-inning comeback, AP reported, citing OptaSTATS. The first three teams to do so went on to win the championship, which is the context in which the Rays' comeback was discussed heading into Game 5.

Milwaukee had been one win from the title entering Game 4, having taken a 3-0 lead in the best-of-seven series. The Rays' win cut that lead to 3-1 and set up Wednesday's game at Tropicana Field.

## The game and reaction

ESPN's game page lists the final score as Brewers 4-1. FOX Sports' highlight package for the game carried the headline that the Brewers had won their first World Series title. FOX also carried comments from Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash reflecting on falling short in the series.

The Rays had been seeking their first championship as well. The result ends both teams' searches in different ways: one franchise wins its first title, and the other goes home without one after a season that included a dramatic extra-inning rescue in Game 4.

## What is not yet confirmed

This story relies on the final score and headline coverage from ESPN and FOX Sports, plus AP's reporting on Game 4. Pitching decisions, box-score lines and any series MVP award are not included here and will be added only once confirmed in an official MLB or AP game account.
